newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah lower, overnight rate fluctuates.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah lower, overnight rate fluctuates.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was lower against the dollar in slow late trading on Tuesday, with call money fluctuating heavily, dealers said.
They said spot rates were adjusting to central bank fixing.
"The market was just going with the fixing. Operators were not surprised," one local bank dealer said.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention rate by one point to 2,338/2,530 and the conversion rate to 2,338/2,386 on Tuesday.
The central bank has depreciated the rupiah by 16 points in the past five weeks. Operators were expecting the central bank to depreciate the rupiah by at least three points this week.
Spot rupiah was at 2,338.0/38.3 at 0915 GMT against an opening of 2,337.25/37.75. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,337.6/37.8 and 2,337.0/37.5, respectively.
But dealers said the market was surprised by the sharp jump in overnight money, which suddenly soared to a high of 38 percent at midday from an opening of 9.0/10.0 percent.
"Some operators seemed to have suffered mismatches and were forced to cover immediately. This hit the market at the wrong time and caused overnight rates to sky-rocket," one said.
Dealers said the brief shock also drove tom/next swap rates up to a high of 0.5/0.6 points from 0.34/0.40 points.
They said tom/next swap relaxed after overnight money fell back to some 20 percent late in the afternoon.
"There are plenty of offers at 20 percent and you hardly can find a buyer now. Tom/next has eased as well," another said.
He said some state banks were seen selling swaps in the morning which pushed six-month swap to a low of 89 points.
Overnight swap was at 0.40/0.45 and tom/next at 0.42/0.50.
One-month swap was at 15.50/16.00, two at 30.5/32.0, three at 46.0/47.5 and six at 90.5/91.0 points.
